newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia minority party said wooing ousted leader.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia minority party said wooing ousted leader.

text.p: Indonesia's Moslem-based minority party is lobbying Megawati Sukarnoputri, ousted leader of the rival Indonesian Democratic Party, for support in its election campaign, a close aide to Megawati said on Wednesday.

The Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are battling the much larger ruling Golkar party for May 29 general elections to the House of Representatives.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, was ousted as the party's leader by a government-backed faction last year, splitting the PDI into two camps.
The PPP sent Mudrick Sangidoe, chief of the party branch in Solo, Central Java, to meet Megawati at her residence on Tuesday, the aide, legislator Soetardjo Soerjogoeritno told Reuters.
Sangidoe asked Megawati to allow her many loyalists in Solo to join the PPP, he said. She gave no commitment but appeared to approve the move, Soerjogoeritno said.
"The meeting should be seen in a broader scope," he said.

"What we know is the decision to send Mudrick to Megawati was made by the PPP's central executive board. The aim of the meeting is to lobby Megawati and her supporters to join the PPP in the election campaign."
PPP officials were not immediately available for comment.
The parties are vying for votes from the 125 million electorate to fill 425 elected seats in the 500-seat House of Representatives. The other 75 seats are alloted to the military which does not vote.
Megawati's faction has not been allowed to contest the poll and she has asked her supporters to boycott the campaign.
But in some cities, many Megawati supporters have joined the PPP's campaign and have been seen carrying her picture.
Soerjogoeritno said the decision by Megawati supporters to join the PPP campaign was an expression of their anger against the government.

PPP chairman Ismail Hasan Metareum was quoted by Kompas newspaper on Wednesday as saying the shift of allegiance was not against the law, adding that people could turn to another party if their aspirations could not be accomodated.
